about: Data, not prose. The orchestrator reads this file to pick a provider for each task. Edit values here to change routing. Nothing in the agent files hardcodes a provider choice.

claude.dispatch: Agent tool with subagent_type (architect, executor, worker, finisher, bug-hunter). Continue with SendMessage.
claude.remainingSource: command-center band or /budget (live 5h and 7d). Use the lower of the two.
claude.verified: 2026-10-03: 5h window 5% used, 7d 53% used (resets 2026-10-08) per orca account list. The 7d window is the binding one. Fable probe OK: Agent tool model=fable answered claude-fable-5-1.

models.fable: claude-fable-5-1. Available (probed 2026-10-03). Use ONLY where a wrong call is expensive: cross-cutting design with no precedent, adversarial review of core scoring/lineup diffs, final whole-branch review, resolving a disagreement between providers. Never for UI wiring, mechanical edits or test runs. Dispatch: Agent(model=fable) or the orchestrator agent. Governor downgrades it to Sonnet at conserve+.
models.opus: claude-opus-5-5. architect agent. Design, specs, proofs, review.
models.haiku: claude-haiku-5-5 (the `haiku` alias; the agent file pins no dated id). finisher.

claude.fableRule: Escalate to fable only when: (1) architect and executor disagree, (2) a core scoring/lineup diff needs a second review after architect, (3) a design touches packages/core types used by 3+ packages. Otherwise prefer sonnet or opus.

codex.remainingSource: node ~/.claude/scripts/provider-usage-report.mjs --json -> codex.primary (usedPct of a windowMinutes window; remaining = 100 - usedPct). Reads Codex's own session logs. Never opens auth.json. Shown in the command-center band and pane.

codex.launchNote: 2026-10-25: worker-start (Codex CLI 0.160.0, update 0.164.0 available) left the brief as an unsubmitted draft under the update banner for ~25 min. Fix: orca terminal read the worker terminal after launch; if the draft is still there, orca terminal send --terminal <h> --enter. Then it started normally.

cursor.remainingSource: node ~/.claude/scripts/provider-usage-report.mjs --json -> cursor.usedPct (monthly) and cursor.buckets. Read from Orca's own account data (the Orca bottom-bar figures). No credentials read here.
cursor.verified: 2026-10-02: Cursor Free monthly cap EXHAUSTED (re-checked 2026-10-03: Cursor Models bucket 100%, Other Models 0% but named models still need a paid plan; no re-probe, it triggers Avast) (Cursor Models bucket 100%, resets 2026-10-19). Auto uses that bucket. A small task costs ~1.5%; a large multi-file UI task (accessibility, ~10 files) consumed the rest. Treat Cursor as available again only after 2026-10-19 or on a paid plan.
cursor.models: Free plan: only 'Auto' works. Checked 2026-10-02: all 24 named models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, Kimi, GLM, Composer) were rejected with 'Free plans can only use Auto'; rejected calls spend no tokens. A paid Cursor plan is needed for a model menu. Fable models are marked NO ZDR (no zero data retention): do not send roster data to them.
cursor.launch: ONLY through Orca (orca orchestration worker-start --agent cursor). Do not spawn cursor-agent directly from scripts or loops: repeated direct spawns trigger the user's Avast.

opencode.dispatch: orca orchestration worker-start --agent opencode2 --worktree current|new-child (no --model). Bind a Run first: orca orchestration run-create --objective <text>. The model comes from opencode.json at the repo root.
opencode.remainingSource: Free OpenCode Zen models. No metered quota is known. Rate limits are unverified.
opencode.verified: 2026-10-15: smoke worker succeeded through Orca (SMOKE-OK, 21s, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free). Micro-eval of 5 free models: all exact on a 6-file search and a signature read. DeepSeek was fastest and cleanest. Edit quality and long context were NOT tested.

models.default: opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free (set in opencode.json). Fastest of five on the micro-eval.
models.reviewer: opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free. A different model family from the default. Used by the reviewer agent.
models.otherFree: big-pickle (slower), mimo-v2.6-flash-free (backticks around answers), step-5-preview-free (slowest, chatty). Others untested.
models.paid: deepseek-v4.1-flash and the rest of the opencode/ list bill the stored account. Never select one without the user's approval.

opencode.agents: .opencode/agents/: scout (read-only), finisher (mechanical), docs-worker (docs/ and README.md only), reviewer (read-only). opencode2 cannot pick an agent or model at launch: the worker runs the default agent, so name the role in the spec or use opencode run --agent from a script.
opencode.dataRule: Free Zen models may retain or train on prompts (Zen terms not verified). Send code, tests and docs only. Probe 2026-10-15: opencode.json read denies are enforced for the read tool (relative and absolute paths), but a grep returned the contents of denied files, and a shell command can read them too. So the denies are a guardrail, not a data barrier. Physical separation helps: data/omniswim.db, data/meets.json, data/backups, data/swimcloud-captures and the pairing token are untracked, so a child worktree does not contain them. These tracked files DO reach a child worktree: data/rosters (1), data/training (2), hsuroster26-27.txt, oburoster202627.txt, possible_hsu_scoringteam2627.txt. Failing tests print swimmer names and times. Keep briefs narrow and run only targeted tests that do not read those files.
opencode.knownIssue: opencode commands run from a non-opencode pane that inherits ORCA_AGENT_HOOK_* env (for example opencode models from a Claude pane) hang with 'Location plugins did not finish activating'. Clear ORCA_AGENT_HOOK_ENDPOINT, ORCA_AGENT_HOOK_PORT and ORCA_AGENT_HOOK_TOKEN for that command. Orca-launched workers are not affected.
opencode.standby: limit-handoff.mjs maps opencode to the Orca agent id opencode2 and skips it when a paid model ran (verified by dry run 2026-10-15). standbyOrder stays empty and available is false, so it is never chosen until the user approves the commit and opts in.
opencode.availableNote: Set true 2026-10-25: the user approved adding OpenCode to the provider pool (redesign plan decision R18), and opencode.json plus .opencode/ are now committed so child worktrees carry the read denies. The deny probe still shows grep and shell can read denied files, so data safety rests on worktree separation: OpenCode workers run ONLY with --worktree new-child, never current. On main after PR #7 the roster text files and data/rosters are untracked; the repo is public, so a child worktree holds nothing that is not already public.
opencode.usage: node ~/.claude/scripts/provider-usage-report.mjs --json -> opencode: sessions, steps, tokens, costUsd, paidModelsUsed (from opencode stats, cached 10 min). No quota %: free models publish none. Shown in the command-center band (oc) and pane.
opencode.launchNote: 2026-10-25: the opencode2 worker ran model "Flint 40B Free", not the opencode.json default, and stopped once on "Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable". A text nudge via orca terminal send resumed it. Check the model line in the terminal after launch.

design.meaning: Schema, algorithm or rule with no precedent. Specs. Proofs.

core.meaning: Scoring, lineup, entry-limit, cut-standard and provenance logic. A wrong value fails silently.

ui.meaning: Component wiring, restyles, accessibility, docs against an existing API.

mechanical.meaning: Lint, typecheck, test runs, narrow edge-case fixes. No design.

adversarial.meaning: Find real defects in code that already passes its tests.

briefTiers.about: How to shape a brief for a target. Source: arXiv:2609.20804 (its weakest model failed most often at finding the file; its stronger models at the patch). The paper tested a plan the model kept itself; orchestrator-written steps for the guided tier are this repo's extension. Templates: the global tiered-brief skill. Checked by the brief-lint hook.

briefMustHave: exact path:start-end locations, read by the orchestrator first
a rule to stop and report when the code is not at the stated lines
the API it may rely on
briefMustNotHave: a scripted implementation (required procedures such as the golden snapshot and the mutation check stay in the acceptance part)
autonomous.tools: a short tools list in the agent file; every tool definition is resent on each request

briefTiers.everyBrief: Run targeted tests while iterating. Run the full gates once at the end. The orchestrator still reruns the full gates before it accepts the report.

rules.unknownBudgetMeans: treat as usable, but say so in the report
rules.parallelEditors: Workers that edit files must have disjoint file scopes, or each gets its own worktree (--worktree new-child). Read-only work may share the current worktree.
rules.coreIsSerial: One editor at a time in packages/core, whatever the provider.
rules.noGitByWorkers: Workers do not commit, branch, merge or push. The orchestrator does, only when the user asks.
rules.reviewerIsNeverBuilder: A diff is reviewed by a different provider than the one that wrote it. If only one provider is available, use a different model tier and say so.
rules.acceptOnlyAfterVerification: The orchestrator reruns the gates and reads the diff before it accepts any worker_done.
rules.quotaBridge: Before routing, run node ~/.claude/scripts/provider-usage-report.mjs --json. remaining = 100 - codex.primary.usedPct; cursor.remainingPct as entered (ignore if isStale). Do not copy these into this file; read them fresh.
rules.noDirectProviderSpawns: Never spawn cursor-agent or codex directly from a script or loop. Use Orca worker-start, one worker at a time.

standbyNote: Order used by limit-handoff.mjs when Claude is out of quota. First provider that is available and below 90% used.
